issues.description: Several solution implementations of the simulate(...) method use the statevector simulator backend (Aer.get_backend("statevector_simulator")) while the exercise specification (and the template docstrings) require returning measurement counts (a histogram / dict[str,int]) for Exercises 2, 3, 4 and 5. Using the statevector simulator for circuits where counts are expected is a structural/runtime mismatch: the statevector backend produces a statevector result (not measurement counts) and executing get_counts on a statevector job is incorrect or will behave differently across Qiskit versions. This discrepancy between the problem intent (return counts) and the concrete backend choice in the solution will confuse students and may produce runtime errors when they try to run or compare with the solution.
issues.suggested_fix: For exercises that must return measurement counts (Exercises 2, 3, 4, 5), run the circuit on a qasm-style simulator (e.g. Aer.get_backend("qasm_simulator")) with an appropriate shots parameter and then call result.get_counts(qc). Alternatively, if you prefer to use the statevector simulator, explicitly sample from the statevector to produce counts (i.e., convert the statevector into probabilities and sample to produce a histogram). Update the solution simulate(...) implementations to use qasm_simulator (or sample from statevector) so the returned type/behavior matches the problem specification.
